title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: amount entered on a notice of loss
content:
## Scope

This rule of the Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims product line fixes the amount entered on a notice of loss for the container named. It reads the declared cargo value on the transport document of the cover's booking and the container count of that booking.

## Rule

1. The amount entered on a notice is the commercial invoice value of the goods in one container of the shipment: the declared cargo value printed on the transport document of the cover's booking recorded for the cover holder, divided by the container count of that booking recorded for the cover holder, rounded to the cent.
2. When either of those records is missing or carries no value, the amount is the cover's insured value divided by the cover's container count, rounded to the cent.
3. The notice amount is the value at risk in the container named. It is not the proven loss, which is fixed only when the claim is settled; the claimant's own quantification of the loss follows with the claim documents.

## Hypothetical worked examples

All figures are hypothetical.

| Records found | Working | Container value |
|---|---|---|
| Transport document declares 250,000.00 USD; booking carries 4 containers | 250,000.00 divided by 4 | 62,500.00 USD |
| No declared cargo value recorded for the cover holder; cover insured for 90,000.00 USD over 7 containers | 90,000.00 divided by 7 is 12,857.142857 | 12,857.14 USD |

## Points of judgement

**The claimant says the damaged goods are worth 3,000.00 USD. Is that the notice amount?** No. The notice carries the value at risk in the container named; the claimant's own quantification follows with the claim documents.

**Which container count divides the declared value?** The container count of the booking recorded for the cover holder, not the number of containers the cover takes; the cover's own count is used only in the fallback of clause 2.
